At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

How do you spark joy in hundreds of millions of people? It starts with a vision - that technology can give voice to stories around the world. In delivering those much-loved stories, Netflix is responsible for a significant portion of global internet traffic.

To steward that responsibility, we work collaboratively with ISPs to deploy Open Connect, Netflix’s Content Delivery Network (CDN), which delivers 100% of Netflix's viewing traffic.  Our team’s mission is to support that delivery by providing an automation and tooling platform that supports the internal operations and external partnerships needed to provide a fantastic viewing experience for all Netflix members.  We are looking for a talented software engineer specializing in infrastructure to join us on that mission.

The Role

You will be charged with handling impactful availability, scalability, and usability challenges and must self-define optimal ways to configure, manage, and observe our growing Open Connect platform. Our platform is a fundamental building block to our streaming initiatives - providing critical solutions for one of the world’s largest CDNs and empowering stakeholders to operate the CDN more efficiently and reliably. In this position, you will have the opportunity to work in a wide variety of areas, such as:

• Implementing microservices to enable analytics, insights, discovery, and visualizations

• Designing orchestration to manage many thousands of globally distributed appliances and devices

• Building data models and APIs to help manage and maintain our fleet

• Understanding the breadth of our multi-tenant platform, creating solutions which can be leveraged across multiple domains - including networking, video, and gaming

You Are

• Someone who likes to work hands-on and self-direct in a fast-paced environment that gives you great freedom and responsibility

• Able to see beyond immediate specifications, can summarize requirements, and architect forward-looking solutions that cross multiple applications

• Capable of working in a highly-collaborative environment alongside your teammates, engineers, Partner Engagement Managers, project managers, and operations teams

• Articulate in communicating opportunities for continuous improvements to existing systems with a clear understanding of the impact on the business.

• Always striving to develop and deploy in measured increments while taking responsibility for the quality of your work.

Required Skills

• 5+ years of expertise in Java, or similar object-oriented language, with confidence and experience in debugging and problem-solving skills

• Deep understanding of cloud architecture and application deployment

• Ability to build and support highly scalable, robust, and fault-tolerant services

• Experience designing, implementing, and debugging systems that interact with large-sized data sets

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Bonus Skills

• Knowledge of CDN architectures and networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, BGP, DNS)

• Experience with multiple data stores and streaming services such as MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch, Cassandra, Kafka, or Redis

• Familiarity with GraphQL or related graph modeling and querying concepts

• Hands-on Big Data experience using Hive, Pig, Hadoop, or similar

• Understanding of front-end technologies including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WebSockets

About the Compute group:

Netflix’s Compute group owns our internet-scale cloud footprint. We constantly innovate to increase fleet-wide agility, efficiency, and reliability of this infrastructure. We build, operate, and maintain Compute services so that Netflix developers can rely on foundational building blocks that enable a “set it and forget it” approach to achieving scalability and cost efficiency. We are responsible for one of the largest Cloud Compute footprints built on AWS, and constantly seeking to push boundaries through innovation to delight hundreds of millions of Netflix users daily.

About the Role:

We are seeking an experienced staff engineer to drive the Compute Runtime team’s charter, guide the team's engineering work, and break new ground through hands-on innovation on the hardest technical challenges. You will be part of the team of engineers responsible for the runtime portion of our Cloud Compute group. The team is responsible for enabling containers to run on our compute nodes as efficiently and reliably as possible. The team owns the Kubernetes data plane software; the container runtime; the way we download and run containers; and the underlying compute node’s operating system. The team partners with many other teams within Netflix to ensure we stay ahead of the business's needs and enable other teams to innovate on top of our platform.

You will be amongst the stunning set of engineers who tackle some of the largest Cloud Compute challenges in the industry. We are moving quickly to support critical business initiatives. You will own key pieces of the Cloud Compute infrastructure and be able to directly trace your work to meaningful business impact, all while working on extremely high-scale systems only found at a handful of companies.

Some examples of the team’s work can be found in tech blogs on “noisy neighbor” detection and mount lock contention.

What you will do:

• Deliver compute platform capabilities and drive adoption across Netflix with a focus on engineering excellence, decisive execution, a spirit of bold experimentation, and tight alignment with business context.

• You are an expert in building scalable and extensible compute platforms, and even better at working with other experts. You form strong cross-functional partnerships driven by trust, embracing a highly aligned and loosely coupled approach with many engineering teams, ensuring our solutions meet their needs while maintaining our focus on agility, scalability, reliability, and efficiency.

• Set the example for operational excellence on the team and across Compute, continuously improving incident response, on-call, and other operational practices.

• Maintain currency on, if not create, industry trends for new architectures, features, and off-the-shelf services; guide the team’s decision-making on incorporating industry trends.

• You recognize industry trends early and stay ahead by developing new architectures, features, and off-the-shelf services, while guiding the team's decisions on when and how to adopt them. Identifying trends matters, but you go further: driven by a passion to learn from and contribute to the open-source world, you keep a pulse on it to shape and forecast the direction of technology.

Desired Skills & Experience:

• A proven track record of architecting and implementing large-scale distributed systems that define and modify infrastructure at 100M+ user scale.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with strong relationship-building ability.

• Passion for technology and the ability to jump into an ambiguous area and break down complex problems.

• Demonstrated technical leadership to empower the team around you and get the most from diverse stakeholders, including product managers, peer engineers across Netflix, and more.

• Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and how to abstract away its complexities.

• Experience with Golang, Java, and/or Python.

• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities effectively.

You will be successful in this role if:

• You enjoy operating in an environment where there are rarely obvious choices, and decision-making requires balancing correctness, speed, and uncertainty. You have opinions but are also open to strong feedback.

• You are able to execute strategically in the short term while thinking long term.

• Have the ability to define and self-manage cross-functional projects fueled by ambiguous questions.

• You take pride in your work, and the work your team delivers, and you always think at a team and business level. You bring an uncomfortably exciting mindset and are comfortable with risk in pursuit of the exceptional.

In 2022 we launched a new lower-priced, ad-supported tier, and we are building an in-house, world-class ad-tech ecosystem to give our members more choice and to offer advertisers a premium, better-than-linear-TV experience. We are looking for the founding members of this new business area for Netflix.

The Ads Forecasting team builds the predictive foundation of the Netflix ads business — the models that tell us, before a campaign ever runs, how much inventory is available and how a campaign will deliver. We forecast supply and demand across audiences, ad products, and formats, and we predict campaign outcomes such as maximum availability, delivery confidence, reach, and frequency, accounting for the ad-serving optimizations that shape delivery. Our forecasts power media planning, underwriting, budget planning, yield, and the public API.

This is a brand-new, foundational role. You will build the machine learning models that augment our simulation-based engine for predicting campaign delivery — turning a slow, rules-based simulation into fast, accurate, learnable models of how campaigns deliver against real inventory. You'll own the modeling and prototyping end-to-end and partner closely with our ML engineering team to take models to production.

In this role, you will:

•
Build, prototype, and iterate on supervised machine learning models that predict campaign delivery outcomes — delivery risk, reach, frequency, and contention — to replace the current simulation engine.

•
Model demand-side campaign outcomes while incorporating supply-side signals, so the models reason about how well available inventory matches what advertisers are trying to achieve (targeting, frequency caps, contention, pacing).

•
Design rigorous offline and online evaluation frameworks to measure model accuracy, robustness to seasonality and distribution shift, and lift over the simulation baseline.

•
Own feature engineering and contribute to the team's feature store — turning ad-serving logs, campaign attributes, and supply signals into reusable, well-documented features.

•
Prioritize explainability and interpretability: your models' outputs must be defensible to sales and media-planning stakeholders making real booking and underwriting decisions.

•
Partner with ML engineers to deploy models at scale and to monitor production model health and drift, feeding monitoring insights back into the next modeling iteration.

•
Collaborate with cross-functional partners across product, engineering, and sales to define objectives, constraints, and trade-offs, and to drive adoption of ML-driven forecasts.

•
Communicate technical decisions, trade-offs, and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences at all levels of the company.

We are looking for:

•
Advanced degree (PhD or Master's) in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.

•
5+ years of relevant experience building machine learning models on large-scale data.

•
Deep expertise in supervised learning (e.g. gradient-boosted trees, regression, and related methods) with a strong bias toward interpretable, explainable models.

•
Strong feature engineering skills and familiarity with feature stores and standard ML lifecycle practice (versioning, evaluation, monitoring, retraining).

•
Proven ability to prototype algorithms and validate them rigorously against production data.

•
Strong programming skills in Python and strong SQL.

•
Working knowledge of ad-serving and campaign concepts — how campaigns are delivered and what creates delivery risk: targeting, frequency caps, contention, bidding, pacing, budget planning, and the core campaign objects/attributes; and the metrics that matter (reach, frequency, impressions, clicks, outcomes). You should understand both the supply side (ad-serving rules and inventory behavior) and the demand side (campaign attributes and advertiser goals). Ads experience is strongly preferred.

•
Ability to work independently, drive your own projects, and make compelling cases for prioritization.

•
Ability to communicate technical and statistical concepts clearly to audiences at many levels.

•
Embodies the Netflix values while bringing a new perspective to continue improving our culture.

Nice to have:

•
Experience at a DSP, SSP, or publisher-side ad platform where predicting campaign outcomes at scale is a core science problem.

•
Familiarity with our ML stack (Metaflow) or comparable large-scale ML tooling.

•
Experience partnering with ML engineers to ship and monitor production ML systems.

•
Experience creating data products, dashboards, or explainability tooling for non-technical stakeholders.

•
Experience applying GenAI to boost developer/research productivity.

Netflix's US Indirect Tax ("ITX") team manages transaction taxes collected from customers and remitted to state and local governments — including sales, use, amusement, communication services, and admissions taxes — as well as property tax, business license tax, and certain gross receipts taxes.

We're looking for an experienced, detail-oriented US Indirect Tax Senior Analyst to own compliance, audit, analytical, and research work across multiple tax types. The ideal candidate has extensive compliance and audit experience and is a self-starter with strong organizational, communication, and process improvement skills.  This is a hands-on role for someone who can successfully execute multiple priorities in parallel, is highly detail-oriented in calculations and writing, and identifies and implements process improvements.

Responsibilities

• Manage sales and use tax audits from notice through resolution, including data gathering, workpaper preparation, exposure analysis, and correspondence with state and local auditors.

• Prepare and review sales/use, gross receipts, business license, and other transaction taxes compliance filings across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.

• Perform Month End accounting reviews, including preparing journal entries for tax reclassification and completing account reconciliations.

• Gather and review information for Unclaimed Property Compliance, including coordinating data deliverables from AP, Payroll, and Production Finance.

• Assist in personal and real property tax compliance, including valuation review and coordination with outside property tax consultants (e.g., appeal filings and support).

• Support personal and real property tax audits, including responding to information requests and evaluating assessment notices.

• Identify and implement process improvements across audit and compliance workflows — including automation opportunities — to reduce manual effort and improve accuracy.

• Research and analyze technical indirect tax issues (e.g., nexus, taxability, sourcing) and summarize conclusions for the team and stakeholders.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Finance, Accounting, Legal, and outside advisors on process improvement projects, audit strategy, business support, and compliance matters.

• Maintain clear, audit-ready documentation and workpapers to support internal review, SOX testing, and external audit requests.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field, is required.

• 5+ years of progressive experience in state and local/indirect tax, including sales/use tax audit and compliance work.

• Strong analytical skills and experience working with large transactional data sets.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage competing audit and compliance deadlines and an array of competing priorities.

• A track record of identifying and driving process improvement in indirect tax operations.

• Excellent communication and project management skills, with the ability to collaborate and manage a variety of competing priorities.

The Team

Netflix’s Business Security Partner (BSP) team is a team of senior security advisors organized around business proximity rather than technical domains. Each BSP partner owns relationships with a defined portfolio of business units, builds long-term relationships with BU leadership, and serves as the security export who understands those businesses well enough to advise on decisions before they are made. We sit in business reviews, participate in architecture conversations, and build the kind of trust with stakeholders that makes security a resource rather than a requirement.

Across all of our relationships, the goal is the same: every major business decision at Netflix should have access to clear, usable security risk context; not a compliance output buried in a document, but actionable guidance from a partner who understands both the risk and the business.

About the Role

This role covers two distinct, fast-moving areas within Netflix: Marketing and Animation.  BSP aligns coverage based on need and often rotates business units. You may cover other areas during your time at Netflix. BSP right-sizes risk while enabling business outcomes.

On the Marketing side, you will be the primary security partner for teams spanning Consumer Products, Brand, Events, Experiences, and Social Media, as well as the external agency and vendor ecosystems that touch pre-release campaign content. You will advise on the security risk of GenAI tools Marketing teams are actively building and adopting, assess vendors and Business Process Outsourcing partners handling sensitive creative assets, and govern the access controls that protect Netflix’s social media accounts.

For Animation, you will partner with Netflix Animation as its dedicated security partner. Your work will span security risk assessment of the animation production pipeline, advancing the alignment of legacy systems with Netflix standards, and advising on architectural decisions that affect how pre-release animated content is protected. The pace of change is high, both in the business and in the legacy integration work. Your ability to engage credibly with engineering and leadership on complex, technically interdependent risk is essential.

This role also carries M&A responsibilities. BSPs at Netflix are expected to support technical security due diligence for acquisitions and subsidiaries.

What You Will Work On:

The Live Ad Insertions team sits at the intersection of broadcast engineering, streaming infrastructure, and digital advertising. Our mission is to deliver a seamless, high-reliability ad insertion experience across live and linear streams, from primetime tentpole events like the NFL and live sports to 24/7 linear feeds and breaking news. We own the full stack of tools, systems, and operational infrastructure required to trigger, stitch, monitor, and verify ad breaks in real time at scale, without compromising the member experience.

Live advertising is one of the highest-stakes, highest-reward surfaces in CTV. When tens of millions of concurrent viewers are watching a single event, there are no second chances. A break happens once, in real time, and the window to act is measured in seconds. That demands more than reliable systems: it demands proactive observability tooling that can detect anomalies before they surface to members, and the ability to make real-time corrections mid-event when something does go wrong. This team operates with the precision of a broadcast NOC and the velocity of a software startup. We are responsible for the technology that turns a live signal into a monetized ad experience, at scale, millisecond by millisecond.

Lead a team of engineers building the real-time infrastructure, tooling, and operational systems for live ad insertion across server-side, client-side, and server-guided delivery models.

Own the reliability and operational excellence of ad insertion during 24/7 linear streams and high-stakes live events, including NFL games, live sports, and awards shows.

•
Define the technical roadmap for live ad insertion, including SCTE signal ingestion and validation, ad pod management, manifest stitching, slate handling, and ad decisioning integration.

•
Partner with ad operations, broadcast engineering, content delivery, and ad serving teams to ensure seamless signal-to-slot execution from ingest to client playback.

•
Drive hiring, retention, and development of a high-performing engineering team capable of operating in a demanding live environment.

•
Establish the on-call and incident response culture for live ad systems, setting SLAs and runbooks for break-glass scenarios during high-profile live events.

Effective communicator across both technical and business stakeholders, including ad sales, ad operations, broadcast engineering, and executive leadership.

Strong track record of hiring and developing senior engineers in competitive talent markets.

Ability to operate in a flat, fast-moving organization, balancing long-term architectural investments against immediate operational needs.

Proven track record of engineering for high-availability, zero-downtime live events, including building operational tooling for ad ops (e.g., real-time fill rate tracking, signal health visualization, and break monitoring workflows).

Vendor Relationships: Experience collaborating with content and distribution partners, including MVPDs, vMVPDs, and broadcast networks, on joint live ad insertion implementations.

North Star & Strategy

•
Define and maintain the target architecture for HR technology across domains

Develop a multi‑year (≈2+ years) architecture roadmap describing how HR systems, integrations, and data models evolve to support business strategy (e.g., growth, new markets, workforce models).

Determine what capabilities sit in 3P platforms versus 1P services.

Decide when to leverage vendor capabilities versus building differentiated 1P experiences.

Assess when to consolidate, sunset, or introduce vendors.

Establish guardrails for configuration vs customization vs 1P extensions within HR platforms.

•
HR data models (e.g. positions, organizations, compensation, locations).

Integrations (APIs, events, batch, and file-based, where necessary).

Identity, entitlements, and access control across HR systems.

Deliver “out‑of‑the‑box” solutions and reusable templates to minimize one‑off integrations and fragile implementations.

•
Define golden sources for HR entities and how data flows into analytics, Finance, Security, and other consumers.

•
Ensure HR data is traceable, auditable, and explainable from original source to reporting and downstream usage.

Non‑Functional Requirements Embedded

•
Embed security, privacy, and regulatory requirements directly into the architecture, including:

•
Regional data residency and cross‑border data transfer considerations.

•
Role‑based access controls and least‑privilege principles.

•
Employee privacy expectations and internal policies.

•
Partner with Security, Privacy, and Legal to convert these requirements into repeatable technical patterns rather than ad‑hoc process overlays.

Translate business outcomes into solution architectures that are sustainable, maintainable, and aligned with long‑term strategy, not just limited by immediate tool configuration options.

Provide architectural direction to engineering teams building 1P services and integrations.

•
Review solution designs and identify approaches that conflict with the target architecture.

•
Enable vertical/domain teams to focus on business needs by ensuring the horizontal foundations are robust and well‑defined.

•
Represent the HR architecture to 3P vendors and partners.

•
Evaluate and, where necessary, challenge vendor proposals that increase complexity, create lock‑in, or duplicate existing 1P capabilities without clear benefit.

Making Trade‑Offs

•
Make explicit, documented decisions on:

•
Short‑term HR needs versus long‑term ecosystem health and simplification.

•
Level of customization versus maintainability, scalability, and upgradeability.

Document decisions and rationale and be prepared to revisit them when new evidence emerges.

Identify opportunities to rationalize redundant tools, platforms, and integrations.

Propose and lead decommissioning efforts for low‑value, high‑cost, or overlapping components.

Champion an architectural approach that reduces complexity, improves reliability, and lowers total cost of ownership across the HR technology landscape.

Deep understanding of at least one major HCM or HR suite (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, etc.), including integrations and extension patterns.

Provide holistic change management strategies across the Finance PMO project portfolio - ensuring that change impacts are assessed, sequenced, and managed at the portfolio level, not just the individual project level.

Lead change management on significant, high-visibility PMO initiatives from end to end: scope change impact assessments, develop and execute communication plans, manage stakeholder engagement, design and oversee training programs, and conduct readiness assessments prior to go-live.

Partner closely with Finance PMO Senior Program Managers and Program Managers to integrate change management activities into project plans, ensuring change is never treated as an afterthought.

Build a culture of high standards - holding the team to rigorous craft while creating the psychological safety needed for iteration and growth.

Manage team capacity across the portfolio; make deliberate prioritization calls when demand exceeds bandwidth and escalate tradeoffs clearly to PMO leadership.

Build change management capability across the broader Finance PMO — coaching program managers and business partners to embed change thinking into their work, extending the team's reach without extending headcount.

Partner with Finance subject matter experts, product teams, and L&D resources to develop high-quality training materials, job aids, and quick-reference guides that support sustainable change.

Gaussian Splatting (GS) is a 3D/4D scene reconstruction technique that enables photorealistic novel-view synthesis with low rendering complexity, making it attractive for deployment on consumer devices such as TVs, streaming sticks, phones, and laptops. Realizing this vision requires addressing several open technical challenges, such as a significant reduction in model training/encoding time and more efficient compression. As part of the Video Algorithms team during this 24-week Fall internship, you will help us investigate the potential of GS as a future streaming format and explore possible improvements, with a focus on building towards a practical system.

Explore GS model compression strategies using open datasets

•
Contribute to early thinking on additional dataset needs for representative scenes.

•
Characterize trade-offs among GS model size, training time, and rendered quality, and quantify the gap relative to streaming-rate targets

•
Identify and experiment with strategies to reduce training/encoding time and/or to improve GS compression efficiency

•
Design and implement a proof-of-concept (PoC) that showcases GS-based rendering on content of interest

The Role

Retail Manager -  Netflix House

Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

Netflix House is a permanent entertainment venue where fans can interact with their favorite Netflix stories through immersive experiences and elevated hospitality. The first two locations will open at King of Prussia in Pennsylvania and Galleria Dallas in 2025. Netflix House is another step in Netflix's commitment to create immersive, in-person experiences for fans around the globe, including NETFLIX BITES Las Vegas, The Queen’s Ball: A Bridgerton Experience; Stranger Things: The Experience; Squid Game: The Experience, now open in New York, Madrid, Sydney and Seoul; and Stranger Things: The First Shadow, now open on London’s West End and coming to Broadway March 28. Netflix has reached 7.5 Million fans across 170 openings in 100 cities and 40 unique formats around the world with an average guest rating of 4.7 out of 5.

As the Retail Manager, you will lead the Fan (guests) and Crew (staff) experience in the retail component of Netflix House. Your responsibilities include oversight of the Retail Associate, Leads, and Crew that are engaging fans, selling merchandise, staffing the main retail space, and smaller pop-up locations while monitoring sales and revenue goals. You will be tasked with overseeing daily staffing plans, hiring, training, and developing the local retail crew. You will partner with our Retail Vendor team, who is the stakeholder in sourcing and purchasing products, ensuring sales revenue is optimized in collaboration with Netflix Corporate strategy. You are an individual who is passionate about sharing Netflix fandom by leading a crew that is set up for success with great training, knowledge, and the right tools to create memorable experiences. The ideal Retail Manager is a communicative leader dedicated to developing and connecting with their team.

This role reports to the Assistant General Manager and is a salaried, on-site role based in King of Prussia, PA.

What you will do:

•
Manage the daily on-site operations and team for the retail store and pop-ups, focusing on sales optimization and fan service informed by revenue targets and budgetary constraints.

•
Partner with Retail Vendor on on-site inventory allocation and replenishment, sales tracking, and overall sales performance.

•
Develop hiring, training, and deployment processes strategies for the retail crew.

•
Optimize ongoing operations to achieve maximum efficiency and best-in-class Fan Service.

•
Work closely with Netflix Corporate resources on operational SOPs, merchandise strategy, and retail trends.

•
Follow the Netflix Corporate visual merchandising strategy in store to ensure a cohesive look across Netflix Houses.

•
Act as a Manager on Duty and Safety on Duty for the operation.

•
Align with the Assistant General Manager and other departments to provide a seamless Fan experience.

•
Promote and foster a mindset of continuous innovation for internal teams and external partners.

What we need from you:

•
Applicants must be at least 18 years of age to be considered for employment.

•
Demonstrated 5+ years of retail store and team management experience.

•
Strong knowledge of hiring practices and training & development strategies.

•
Strong knowledge of retail trends in the Location Based Entertainment (LBE) industry, preferred.

•
Experience managing direct and indirect teams in an environment that embraces continual learning and change.

•
Demonstrated experience in overseeing daily activities, enforcing EHS compliance, managing staff training, and optimizing workflows to enhance both safety and guest experience to ensure an overall safe, efficient, and guest-focused operation.

•
Excellent communication skills, both verbal and digital.

•
Excellent leadership skills.

•
Strong desire to think outside the box and innovate.

•
Availability to work days, nights, weekends, and holidays in a 365-day attraction.

Generally, our compensation structure consists solely of an annual salary; we do not have bonuses. You choose each year how much of your compensation you want in salary versus stock options. To determine your personal top of market compensation, we rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience to determine your compensation in the market range. The range for this role is $127,000.00 - $171,000.00.

Inclusion is a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you need an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner.

This role is specifically focused on enabling our security teams in detecting and mitigating various types of security risks affecting our expansive cloud technology footprint. This requires a holistic understanding of our infrastructure topology, access controls, security policies and usage patterns.
